purpose: Validate actual CPU-time measurement and compare it with elapsed time on frozen generic span-page-reuse experiment builds. This is a separate follow-up panel, not a relabeling of the older wall-time-only campaign.
unit_tests:
✔ guest identities retain RAM versions and reject non-address names (1.003134ms)
✔ time weighting preserves distinct stacks and modules; labels do not alter samples (1.2818ms)
✔ task identity handles parentheses in Linux comm (1.210553ms)
✔ CPU deltas exclude elapsed waiting and preserve nanosecond differences (0.611871ms)
✔ process churn and recycled task IDs cannot masquerade as complete CPU totals (0.864396ms)
✔ counter resets are flagged instead of reporting negative CPU time (0.199974ms)

limits: CPU seconds exclude time descheduled/asleep, but not frequency, cache, JIT or active-contention variability.
Process snapshots have polling/collection margins around guest execution; CPU-thread work is bounded by existing pause and stop points.
Busiest-thread identity is confirmed by the trace in one diagnostic Snakes run. Throughput runs do not profile, and the busiest thread label alone does not prove identity.
Two runs per variant per game are a small panel. All observations are retained; do not use means alone as proof of speedup.
No owned diagnostic/test/build workload overlapped throughput runs; outside host activity was uncontrolled.
The underlying optimization remains unadopted. This follow-up changes the measurement harness, not the emulator.
